title: Active Learning of Conditional Generative Models via the Transport Neural Tangent Kernel
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: Selecting inputs by distributional sensitivity beats mean-based and random selection on total, mean, and shape error as data grows.
layout: 4 panels in a row: density plot, then three line plots; shared legend below
description: A single-row figure with four panels. Panel A is a heatmap of a ground-truth conditional density p(y|x) over x from 0 to 1. The purple density is narrow at the edges and bulges into a bimodal shape around x=0.5. A dashed black line marks the conditional mean, and white dotted curves mark the modes. Panels B, C and D are line plots of log test error against the number of observations, from 5 to 10. B shows total W2 error, C shows mean error, and D shows shape error. Each plot has three curves with shaded bands: Random in black, Mean AL in blue, and Wasserstein AL in red. All three curves decline. The red curve falls fastest and is lowest in B and D. In C it roughly matches or beats the blue curve. A legend runs along the bottom.
caption: Synthetic conditional density estimation. (A) Ground truth conditional density $\mu(x)$. (B--D) Test error after active learning as a function of training set size: total risk (B), mean prediction error (C), and shape error (D). Results averaged over $50$ random initializations; shaded bands show $\pm 2$ standard errors.
abstract: Many high-throughput scientific experiments produce distributional outputs, requiring conditional generative models to interpret the data, and to predict outcomes at new inputs. Acquiring experimental data at new conditions (e.g., for a new antigen or a new cell type) is often expensive, motivating the need for automated experimental design methods. However, existing active learning frameworks are limited as they assume scalar or vector-valued outputs. We first show that the Wasserstein test risk of a conditional generative task decomposes into a mean term and a shape term, demonstrating why mean-based active learning is blind to distributional shape. To capture both, we propose the transport Neural Tangent Kernel (tNTK), a tractable kernel that measures how sensitive a generative model's predicted distribution is with respect to its parameters. The tNTK recovers the standard NTK in the deterministic limit and upper-bounds the posterior FrÃ©chet variance of the prediction under small parameter perturbations. It admits a closed-form expression for affine Gaussian transport and tractable Monte Carlo estimators otherwise. Treating the tNTK as the covariance function of a Gaussian process, we greedily select inputs that minimize the total GP posterior variance across the pool, yielding a distribution-aware active learning strategy. We evaluate this strategy across four classes of conditional generative models, including conditional flow matching and conditional Monge gap, on synthetic distributions, intent-labeled sentences, and single-cell perturbation responses. In these experiments, the tNTK outperforms the baseline NTK computed from the conditional mean, demonstrating the value of distribution-aware active learning for generative-modeling tasks.
